stepNotes.1: The unit divides loopback binding/origins, Host/RP derivation, Origin/cookie/WebSocket checks, stale tunnel blocking, and response headers.
stepNotes.2: Local browser and process attackers motivate DNS-rebinding, proxy spoofing, cross-site WebSocket, UI-session, stale-tunnel, and framing defenses.
stepNotes.3: Only loopback binds and matching Host-derived loopback Origins pass; forwarded headers are ignored and WebSocket/passkey consumers reuse the same policy.
stepNotes.4: Per-request work is fixed-size parsing/header setting, and tunnel scanning is one startup pass over a small run directory.
stepNotes.5: Bind, identity, authorization, response, and legacy-process responsibilities are cohesive and integrated through narrow functions.
stepNotes.6: Four catches are malformed-state cleanup or rejected-socket teardown; they are fail-closed/best-effort and already tracked as Low.
stepNotes.7: Nineteen direct tests cover spoofing, aliases, stale public origins, tunnels, and framing; cookie/socket/local-host and real WebSocket rebinding cases remain gaps.
stepNotes.8: Only the deferred Low catch finding applies, no new finding was accepted, and no Critical re-verification file is required.
stepNotes.9: All four security test files passed 19 tests; listening-server adversarial integration remains the next meaningful gate.
